question: A family has two children. What is the probability that both children are boys given that at least one of them is a boy born on a Monday? (Assume equal probability for births on all days.)
explanation:
Sample space: Each child has 2 genders × 7 days = 14 options. So, number of pairs = $14 \times 14 = 196$.

Number of ways both are boys: $7 \times 7 = 49$.

Number of ways at least one is a boy born on Monday:
First child is boy on Mon: 7 possibilities for second child = 14.
Second child is boy on Mon: 7 for first child = 14.
Subtract both are boy on Mon: 1 case (counted twice).
So total = $14 + 14 - 1 = 27$.

Number of cases where both are boys and at least one is born on Monday:
First boy on Mon: 7 choices for second (any day) = 7.
Second on Mon: 7 choices for first = 7.
Subtract both on Mon (counted twice): 1.
So $7 + 7 - 1 = 13$.

$P(\text{Both boys}|\text{at least one is boy on Mon}) = \frac{13}{27}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\dfrac{13}{27}}$.
